newsitem.title: USA: NY broker sues Saudi Prince over hotel sale.
newsitem.headline: NY broker sues Saudi Prince over hotel sale.

text.p: A real estate broker said on Thursday he was suing a Saudi prince for allegedly refusing to pay him a commission of almost $10 million when the prince bought New York's Plaza Hotel two years ago.

The suit alleged that Prince Alwalid Bin Talal Bin Abduhlaziz Al Saud and associates created their own brokerage company to avoid paying the $9.75 million fee. It accuses the prince of failing to license the firm as required by the law.

Broker Lawrence Russo said in the complaint filed in New York State Supreme Court on Tuesday that he was seeking $38.8 million in damages against the prince for the fraudulent use of an unlicensed broker.

"It appears that in an effort to save himself the brokerage fee on the deal, Prince Alwalid created his own company and listed it as the broker for the sale," Russo's lawyer Barry Slotnick said. "We charge that he did this with the specific intention of capturing the brokerage fee for himself."

A spokesman for Russo's company P.H. Capital Corporation said Citibank, which owned the landmark Fifth Avenue hotel through one of its subsidiaries, had authorised the broker in 1992 to attempt to sell it. He said Russo contacted the prince and his associates in 1994 and provided them with the information they needed to negotiate the deal.
The prince and his associates later met with Citibank and completed the deal as it had been structured by Russo, according to P.H. Capital Corp.

The prince, a nephew of Saudi King Fahd, paid $325 million for the hotel in 1995. He also has stakes in Citicorp, EuroDisney, Four Seasons Hotels, Fairmount Hotels and Saks Fifth Avenue department store.
